newsitem.title: UK: OPRAF/Railtrack to move on West Coast line.
newsitem.headline: OPRAF/Railtrack to move on West Coast line.

text.p: Britain's state-run Office of Passenger Rail Franchising and the privately-owned rail infrastructure company Railtrack Plc said they would make a statement about the West Coast main line on Tuesday.

A OPRAF spokesman said that a news conference planned for 1100 GMT would make "an important announcement on the future of the West Coast Main Line" (WCML), one of two main North-South express railway lines linking major cities in Great Britain.

While OPRAF has been working on plans to franchise the WCML operation as one of 25 train operating companies in Britain due for privatisation, Railtrack has been working on a plan for a huge upgrade of the line which could cost up to 900 million stg.
The two bodies said last month they had been discussing how it might be possible to combine the infrastrucutre renewal with passenger service upgrades over the coming years.

Industry sources said that the most likely announcement today would be that broad terms had been agreed to allow the forthcoming WCML franchise contract to include provision for a new operator to acquire high-speed trains, and improve existing services, alongside the seven-to-eight year line renewal plan.
WCML is thus set to be one of the largest and most complex franchise contracts in the passenger privatisation process.
